items.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024
items.q: I just think the guy is incredible. You know so many people, he made those instruction books, those play-a-long tapes.

ctx.x: Have you ever had a student at one of these perhaps workshops ask you if you use a particular jazz technique and you don’t really know what they’re talking about? I mean it’s happened to me. Something that they’ve learned from a book or some video on YouTube. So when do you use that?

Yeah. Well I have to be honest, you know if I’m aware of something. You know to give you an example, Jamey Aebersold, Like Jamey Aebersold — look what Jamey Aebersold has done for the jazz world. I just think the guy is incredible. You know so many people, he made those instruction books, those play-a-long tapes. He has like created a forum for so many people that are just like — if they’re amateurs, if they’re young students — to get their skills together. To get their confidence up. Even if you could — to go to…

Yeah. So you’re at a cocktail party and somebody who’s fairly well off gets to know you a little bit. And they say, “So Jane, my niece is a good saxophone player and she wants to be a jazz musician. What do you think about that? What should she do?”
